intent: One airfield in the Midlands: the date and the king, Farina's Alfa, the 7-vs-24 split, then the racing car riding the line to Monza where the first title was decided.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Which track held the FIRST Formula 1 championship race?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Which track held the first Formula 1 championship race?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: Silverstone. On 13 May 1950 a former bomber airfield in England staged the first World Championship race.

lines.direction: tighten on the airfield; a crown sticker on 'King'; the FARINA card and a racing car sticker on 'Farina'; a trophy on 'title' as the British flag-ball grins and the UK pulses
lines.text: King George watched from the stands. Giuseppe Farina won in an Alfa Romeo, then took the first title.

lines.direction: ease back over England; the THEN / NOW split lands on 'rounds' (7 vs 24); a calendar sticker on 'calendar'; the Italian flag-ball thinks on 'finale'; the split folds at the end
lines.text: That season had 7 rounds. This year's calendar runs to 24, with the finale weeks away.

lines.direction: pull right out so England and Italy share the frame; a racing car rides the drawn line from Silverstone to Monza until 'Monza'; the Monza pin and tag; a chequered flag on 'runways' as the UK pulses
lines.text: Farina clinched it at Monza. The British Grand Prix still runs on the old runways.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: From bombers to Grands Prix. Follow us.
